ben: Quick dump from the afternoon load test. Seeing repeated 100-250ms tail spikes during long-context runs. Suspect eviction-policy oscillation + KV fragmentation causing pager thundering. Attaching short profiling snippets and flame links.

ben: flamegraph: https://internal.perf/fgs/3109876543-kv-fifo-longctx.svg
ben: pprof counters (sample):
```
pager_evictions/sec: 1842
kv_reinsert/sec: 912
avg_reclaim_ms: 14.7
avg_token_latency_ms (tail): 180
kv_frag_pct: 37.2
kv_miss_rate: 0.29
```
Notably this run used `--evict=fifo` and `--hotset=0.18`.

cara: Oof. FIFO under sustained long contexts then? Did you compare with LRU run copies? :thinking:

ben: Yup. LRU run had ~30% fewer evictions overall, but we saw steady memory growth on very long prefixes (reuse hole regression). FIFO gave more deterministic reclaim but fragmentation % blew up and we hit paging. Also saw kernel-selection flips in the same windows: packed-attn kernel -> generic kernel -> slower path, which added ~3-5ms per token when pager was active.

dan: That kernel flip is interesting. My hypothesis: large kv-miss bursts shrink the effective batch size and widen seq-len distribution, our kernel selector then chooses safer generic kernels. Combined with page faults from fragmentation, that multiplies the latency. We should make kernel selection aware of `kv_miss_rate` or prefer packed kernel for steady throughput even with some misses.

alice: I reproduced locally. Repro script: `scripts/repro_long_ctx.sh --model=redwood-1-small --seq=8192 --clients=12 --evict=fifo --duration=10m`
Log excerpt where spikes line up with reclaim events:
```
[00:03:42] token_latency_ms: 14.2
[00:03:43] token_latency_ms: 198.7  <-- spike
[00:03:43] pager_reclaim: 115 entries
[00:03:43] kv_fragmentation_pct: 39.1
[00:03:44] kernel: switched -> generic_kernel_v2
```

deploy-bot: :warning: Canary svc/kv-pager paused: observed latency >150ms for 3 consecutive minutes (rule: pager-latency-threshold).

ben: Proposed mitigations: 1) add an in-place compaction pass to coalesce free slots when `kv_frag_pct > 30%` (run off hotpath, rate-limited), 2) add hysteresis on eviction-policy switching (prevent flip-flop LRU<->FIFO within 5m), 3) make kernel selector consider `kv_miss_rate`/`kv_frag_pct` signals so we avoid switching to generic kernel if that will trigger CPU+page-fault path. Also add an emergency fallback that reduces batch size gracefully instead of full kernel swap.

cara: Also add `kv_frag_pct` and `kv_miss_rate` to Console per-route dashboards and alert at 25%+ so SRE sees it before the bot pauses canary. :eyes:

dan: I'll open a PR to add compaction + metric emission + selector tweak. Assigning @ben for review and perf validation. Will include microbenchmark and stress harness.

dan: PR draft: `github.com/redwood-inference/rt/compare/kv-compaction-3109` (WIP)

ben: :thumbsup: I'll add unit tests and a stress scenario in our load harness. Also will try an experiment: keep eviction policy FIFO but do a periodic compaction every 30s during long-context flows and see tail improvement.

cara: Thanks team — let's try to get a quick canary with compaction off by default, metric only, then enable compaction behind feature flag. If results look good we can tune hysteresis thresholds.

alice: Noted. I'll run extended 1h stress with the compaction branch once PR lands and paste updated flamegraphs.

ben: Cool. I'll follow up with a short RFC for kernel-selector heuristics so it's not ad-hoc.
